learn.title: Two equations at once
learn.body: A system of equations is two or more equations that share the same letters. A solution must satisfy all of them. For two lines, that is the point where they cross.

learn.title: Solve $y=x+1$ and $y=-x+3$
learn.body: Graph both and find where they meet.

learn.title: Three possible outcomes
learn.body: Two lines can cross once (one solution). They can be parallel (no solution). Or they can be the same line (infinitely many solutions).

learn.title: Compare slopes
steps: So the lines are parallel and there is no solution.

learn.body: Graphing is quick but can be inexact when the crossing is not on a grid point. Algebra, in the next lessons, gives exact answers.

questions.prompt: What is the solution of a system of two lines?
questions.explanation: A solution makes both equations true at once, so it lies on both lines.

questions.prompt: Lines $y=2x-1$ and $y=x+2$ cross at $x=3$. What is $y$ there?
Parallel lines never meet, so the system has no \_\_
questions.explanation: There is no point on both lines.

questions.prompt: How many solutions do $y=2x+1$ and $y=2x+4$ have?
questions.explanation: Same slope, different intercepts: parallel lines that never meet.

questions.prompt: How many solutions do $y=x+2$ and $2y=2x+4$ have?
questions.explanation: Divide the second by 2: $y=x+2$. It is the same line, so every point on it is a solution.

questions.prompt: Solve a system by graphing. Put the steps in order.
steps: Graph the second line on the same axes
Read the crossing point and check it in both equations
questions.explanation: Always check the point in both equations, because a graph can be misread.
